To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a new model for link scheduling in wireless networks and we have proposed algorithms to solve this problem.

(1) we develop a novel interference-aware link scheduling algorithm for wireless networks that uses time slots within a factor of two of the optimum, (2) we present an efficient algorithm for the distributed case that uses a constant factor of slots within a factor two of the optimum and requires only a constant number of communications per slot, and (3) our theoretical results are corroborate by simulations.

(i) the throughput of a static wireless network can be maximized by efficient TDMA link scheduling, (ii) the throughput of the wireless network can be further improved by allowing a node to adjust its transmission power, and (iii) the throughput improvement is more significant when the interference range of a node is larger than its transmission range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of efficient link scheduling for wireless networks.
the fundamental issue of how to schedule the transmissions in a static multi-hop wireless network to maximize the throughput, and we develop efficient algorithms to solve the problem.

the interference-aware scheduling problem is tractable, and can be efficiently solved using both centralized and distributed approaches.
